chose: 2.8 CONTRACT (merge-stable supersession, MOAT.md P0).
(a) SCHEMA: decision_logged and memory_promoted each gain optional `supersedes_id`, the event id (ULID) of the entry `supersedes` names. The writer stamps it and agents never pass it. It is valid only alongside `supersedes`. The fingerprint is re-emitted. Older readers ignore unknown top-level fields, so a pre-2.8 reader keeps today's ordinal behaviour.
(b) WRITER: ToolContext.appendAndProject (the only mutation path: MCP, batched write-back, CLI) stamps it from its own fold when the handle resolves: a decision at that ordinal in this record, or a memory in the named record. A handle that does not resolve (forward, self, unknown) stays unstamped and inert, as today. A caller-supplied supersedes_id that differs from the derived one is refused. Each batch append advances the fold, so a decision superseding an earlier one in the same batch gets that decision's real id.
(c) FOLD: a supersession carrying an id resolves by id among entries already folded, never by ordinal. An id that names no folded entry (voided, or absent) is inert. In state, `supersedes` becomes the resolved handle (D<current ordinal>), so projections name the decision actually replaced. Without an id, it resolves by ordinal, as before. Memories do the same within a record, and doctor's cross-record memory retirement resolves by id when present.
(d) SCOPE TIER: guards.json and labels.json apply the same rule. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bumps.
(e) OUT OF SCOPE:
- verification_recorded.decision. Coverage also needs the same command and tree fingerprint (driver/drive.ts), so a renumbered handle can only cause a re-run.
- Judge subjects (typed-judge).
- D<n> in prose and docs (note 01M341NV needs an operator ruling).
- Events logged before 2.8 keep ordinal resolution.
(f) rust-core mirrors this as 2.9.
PREDICT: the MOAT.md §4 repro ends with B's refund rule and A's per-entity rule in force and A's calendar-year rule retired. Every log without a merge-induced renumber folds and projects byte-identically.
over: Accepting a ULID in `supersedes` itself: pre-2.8 validators reject a non-D<n> value and would drop the whole decision for older readers. A fold-only fix: the log records no branch lineage, so no ordinal rule can recover the intended target. Stamping in each writer (three copies instead of the one mutation path). Falling back to the ordinal when an id does not resolve (that ordinal is exactly what a merge moved). Including verification_recorded (safe-failing, and it widens the schema for no correctness gain).
because: D<n> is a position in ULID order. A union merge of two branches that both logged decisions, or a correction that voids one, shifts it. The fold then retires whatever now holds that position. The repro silently retired a teammate's standing rule and left the intended target in force beside its replacement. Event ids never move, and the writer knows the target at write time, so stamping the id there fixes every future supersession without changing what agents type.
